units.zh: 魏觀，字杞山，蒲圻人。
units.en: Wei Guan, whose style was Qishan, came from Puqi.
units.literal: Wei Guan, styled Qishan, was a native of Puqi.

units.zh: 元季隱居蒲山。
units.en: In the closing years of the Yuan dynasty he withdrew to live in seclusion on Pu Mountain.
units.literal: At the end of the Yuan he lived in seclusion on Pu Mountain.

units.zh: 太祖下武昌，聘授國子助教，再遷浙江按察司僉事。
units.en: After the Founding Emperor captured Wuchang, Guan was summoned and made an assistant instructor at the Directorate of Education, then promoted to vice commissioner of the Zhejiang surveillance commission.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor took Wuchang, he was invited and appointed Assistant Instructor at the Directorate of Education, then was transferred again to Vice Commissioner of the Zhejiang Surveillance Commission.

units.zh: 吳元年，遷兩淮都轉運使。
units.en: In the first year of the Wu regime he was appointed director of transport for the Two Huai region.
units.literal: In the first year of Wu he was transferred to Director of Transport for the Two Huai.

units.zh: 入為起居註。
units.en: He was brought into the capital as recorder of imperial actions.
units.literal: He entered service as Recorder of Imperial Actions.

units.zh: 奉命偕吳琳以幣帛求遺賢於四方。
units.en: On imperial command he joined Wu Lin in traveling the realm with gifts of silk and cloth to seek out neglected men of talent.
units.literal: By order he accompanied Wu Lin, bearing silks and gifts to seek out lost worthies in every quarter.

units.zh: 洪武元年，建大本堂，命侍太子說書及授諸王經。
units.en: In Hongwu 1 the Great Foundation Hall was established, and he was charged with attending the crown prince in classical instruction and teaching the imperial princes.
units.literal: In the first year of Hongwu the Great Foundation Hall was built, and he was ordered to attend the crown prince in lecturing on the classics and to instruct the princes in the classics.

units.zh: 未幾，又命偕文原吉、詹同、吳輔、趙壽等分行天下，訪求遺才，所舉多擢用。
units.en: Soon afterward he was again sent out with Wen Yuanji, Zhan Tong, Wu Fu, Zhao Shou, and others to scour the empire for overlooked talent; most of their nominees were raised to office.
units.literal: Before long he was again ordered, together with Wen Yuanji, Zhan Tong, Wu Fu, Zhao Shou, and others, to travel the realm in separate parties seeking out neglected talent; most of those they recommended were promoted and employed.

units.zh: 三年，轉太常卿，考訂諸祀典。
units.en: In the third year he became minister of ceremonies and undertook a systematic review of the state ritual codes.
units.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Minister of Ceremonies and examined and revised the various sacrificial regulations.

units.zh: 稱旨，改侍讀學士，尋遷祭酒。
units.en: The Emperor was pleased with his work and made him a reader-in-waiting, then shortly afterward promoted him to libationer of the Directorate of Education.
units.literal: His work pleased the Emperor, and he was changed to Reader-in-Waiting, then soon promoted to Libationer.

units.zh: 明年坐考祀孔子禮不以時奏，謫知龍南縣，旋召為禮部主事。
units.en: The following year he was punished for failing to submit his review of Confucian temple rites on schedule and was demoted to magistrate of Longnan County, but was soon recalled as a principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites.
units.literal: The next year, on a charge of reporting the examination of Confucian sacrificial rites not at the proper time, he was demoted to magistrate of Longnan county, then soon recalled as a principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites.

units.zh: 五年，廷臣薦觀才，出知蘇州府。
units.en: In the fifth year court officials recommended Guan's ability, and he was appointed prefect of Suzhou.
units.literal: In the fifth year court ministers recommended Guan's talent, and he was sent out as prefect of Suzhou.

units.zh: 前守陳寧苛刻，人呼「陳烙鐵」。
units.en: His predecessor Chen Ning had ruled with harsh severity, and the people nicknamed him "Iron Brand Chen."
units.literal: The previous prefect Chen Ning was harsh and exacting; people called him "Iron Brand Chen."

units.zh: 觀盡改寧所為，以明教化、正風俗為治。
units.en: Guan reversed everything Ning had put in place and made his administration a project of moral instruction and the reform of local custom.
units.literal: Guan completely changed what Ning had done, taking clarification of teaching and transformation and correction of customs as his governing principle.

units.zh: 建黌舍。
units.en: He founded a school.
units.literal: He built a school hall.

units.zh: 聘周南老、王行、徐用誠，與教授貢潁之定學儀；
units.en: He engaged Zhou Nanlao, Wang Xing, and Xu Yongcheng, and together with the instructor Gong Yingzhi drew up the school's ceremonial regulations;
units.literal: He engaged Zhou Nanlao, Wang Xing, and Xu Yongcheng, and together with Instructor Gong Yingzhi fixed the school ceremonies;

units.zh: 王彜、高啟、張羽訂經史；
units.en: Wang Yi, Gao Qi, and Zhang Yu edited the classical and historical texts;
units.literal: Wang Yi, Gao Qi, and Zhang Yu revised the classics and histories;

units.zh: 耆民周壽誼、楊茂、林文友行鄉飲酒禮。
units.en: and the village elders Zhou Shouyi, Yang Mao, and Lin Wenyou presided over the community drinking rites.
units.literal: the elders Zhou Shouyi, Yang Mao, and Lin Wenyou conducted the village drinking ceremony.

units.zh: 政化大行，課績為天下最。
units.en: His policies took deep root, and his administrative rating ranked first in the empire.
units.literal: Government and transformation were carried out on a grand scale, and his performance rating was the highest in the realm.

units.zh: 明年擢四川行省參知政事。
units.en: The following year he was promoted to vice administrator of the Sichuan branch secretariat.
units.literal: The next year he was promoted to Vice Administrator of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat.

units.zh: 未行，以部民乞留，命還任。
units.en: Before he could leave, the populace petitioned to keep him, and the throne ordered him to resume his post.
units.literal: Before he departed, because the people of his department begged that he remain, he was ordered to return to his post.

units.zh: 初，張士誠以蘇州舊治為宮，遷府治於都水行司。
units.en: Earlier, Zhang Shicheng had turned Suzhou's old government compound into a palace and relocated the prefectural offices to the waterways directorate.
units.literal: Earlier, Zhang Shicheng had taken the old seat of government in Suzhou as his palace and moved the prefectural seat to the Directorate of Waterways.

units.zh: 觀以其地湫隘，還治舊基。
units.en: Finding the new site damp and cramped, Guan moved the government back to its former location.
units.literal: Guan, because that site was low-lying and cramped, returned administration to the old foundations.

units.zh: 又浚錦帆涇，興水利。
units.en: He also dredged the Brocade Sail Canal and undertook hydraulic works.
units.literal: He also dredged the Brocade Sail Canal and promoted water conservancy.

units.zh: 或譖觀興既滅之基。
units.en: Someone accused him of rebuilding on ground associated with a defeated regime.
units.literal: Someone slandered Guan for raising foundations already destroyed.

units.zh: 帝使御史張度廉其事，遂被誅。
units.en: The Emperor dispatched Censor Zhang Du to investigate on the spot, and Guan was put to death.
units.literal: The Emperor sent Censor Zhang Du to investigate the matter on the spot, and Guan was thereupon executed.

units.zh: 帝亦尋悔，命歸葬。
units.en: The Emperor soon came to regret the decision and ordered Guan's remains sent home for burial.
units.literal: The Emperor also soon regretted it and ordered that his body be returned for burial.

units.zh: 陶垕仲，名鑄，以字行，鄞人。
units.en: Tao Houzhong, whose personal name was Zhu and who was known by his style Houzhong, came from Yin.
units.literal: Tao Houzhong, personal name Zhu, styled by his courtesy name, was a native of Yin.

units.zh: 洪武十六年，以國子生擢監察御史。
units.en: In Hongwu 16 he was raised from the ranks of Directorate students to investigating censor.
units.literal: In the sixteenth year of Hongwu, as a student of the Directorate of Education he was selected and promoted to Investigating Censor.

units.zh: 糾彈不避權貴。
units.en: In his impeachments he showed no deference to the powerful.
units.literal: In impeachment he did not avoid the powerful and noble.

units.zh: 劾刑部尚書開濟至死，直聲動天下。
units.en: He impeached the minister of justice Kai Ji on a capital charge, and his fearless reputation resounded throughout the empire.
units.literal: He impeached Minister of Justice Kai Ji to the death penalty, and his upright reputation shook the realm.

units.zh: 未幾，擢福建按察使。
units.en: Before long he was appointed surveillance commissioner of Fujian.
units.literal: Before long he was promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of Fujian.

units.zh: 誅贓吏數十人，興學勸士，撫恤軍民。
units.en: He executed dozens of corrupt officials, revived schooling and encouraged scholars, and looked after both soldiers and civilians.
units.literal: He executed several tens of corrupt officials, promoted schools and encouraged scholars, and comforted and relieved soldiers and civilians.

units.zh: 帝下詔褒異。
units.en: The Emperor issued an edict singling him out for praise.
units.literal: The Emperor issued an edict praising him as extraordinary.

units.zh: 布政使薛大方貪暴，垕仲劾奏之。
units.en: When administrative commissioner Xue Dafang proved greedy and brutal, Houzhong impeached him.
units.literal: Administrative Commissioner Xue Dafang was greedy and violent; Houzhong impeached and memorialized against him.

units.zh: 大方辭相連，並逮至京。
units.en: Dafang's testimony implicated others in turn, and they were all brought to the capital for trial.
units.literal: Dafang's words implicated others in succession, and they were all seized and brought to the capital.

units.zh: 訊實，坐大方罪，詔垕仲還官。
units.en: The inquiry confirmed the charges; Dafang was convicted, and Houzhong was ordered back to his post.
units.literal: On investigation the facts were established; Dafang was convicted, and an edict ordered Houzhong restored to office.

units.zh: 垕仲言：「臣父昔為方氏部曲，以故官例徙鳳陽。
units.en: Houzhong memorialized, "My father had once served in the Fang clan's forces and, under the usual rule for such men, was relocated to Fengyang.
units.literal: Houzhong said: "My father was formerly a follower of the Fang clan; by the precedent for such officials he was relocated to Fengyang.

units.zh: 臣幼弱，依兄撫養，至於有成。
units.en: I was a small child and was raised by my elder brother until I came of age.
units.literal: I was young and weak and relied on my elder brother to rear and nurture me until I came of age.

units.zh: 今兄亦為鳳陽軍吏。
units.en: My brother now serves there as a military clerk as well.
units.literal: Now my brother is also a military clerk at Fengyang.

units.zh: 臣叨聖恩，備位司憲。
units.en: I have been favored with the sage Emperor's grace and now hold office as a surveillance official.
units.literal: I have received the sagely grace and hold a post in the surveillance service.

units.zh: 欲推祿養報生育恩，使父母兄弟得復聚處，實戴聖天子孝治天下至意。」
units.en: I wish to use my salary to repay those who raised me and to bring my parents and brothers together again—truly reflecting the sage Emperor's purpose of governing the realm through filial devotion."
units.literal: I wish to extend my salary to support and repay the grace of those who bore and reared me, so that father, mother, and brothers may again dwell together—truly bearing the sagely Son of Heaven's utmost intent in governing the realm through filial piety."

units.zh: 帝特許迎養，去徙籍。
units.en: The Emperor granted the request, allowed him to bring his family for support, and struck his name from the relocation register.
units.literal: The Emperor specially permitted him to bring his parents for support and removed him from the relocation register.

units.zh: 垕仲清介自持，祿入悉以贍賓客。
units.en: Houzhong lived with austere integrity and spent his entire salary entertaining guests.
units.literal: Houzhong was pure and self-restrained; his entire salary income he used to support guests.

units.zh: 未幾，卒官。
units.en: Before long he died in office.
units.literal: Before long he died in office.

units.zh: 時廣西僉事王佑，泰和人。
units.en: At that time Wang You, a vice commissioner in Guangxi, came from Taihe.
units.literal: At that time Vice Commissioner Wang You of Guangxi was a native of Taihe.

units.zh: 按察使尋適嘗咨以政體。
units.en: The surveillance commissioner Xun Shi once sought his counsel on the fundamentals of administration.
units.literal: Surveillance Commissioner Xun Shi once consulted him on the substance of government.

units.zh: 佑曰：「蠻方之人瀆倫傷化，不及此時明禮法、示勸懲，後難治」適從之，廣西稱治。
units.en: You replied, "The people of these frontier regions violate moral order and corrupt custom; unless ritual and law are made clear and rewards and punishments displayed now, they will be difficult to govern later." Xun Shi followed his advice, and Guangxi came to be known as well governed.
units.literal: You said: "People in the barbarian regions violate ethics and harm customs; if ritual and law are not clarified and encouragement and punishment displayed at this time, it will be hard to govern later." Shi followed this, and Guangxi was said to be well governed.

units.zh: 蜀平，徙佑知重慶州。
units.en: After Sichuan was pacified, You was transferred to serve as prefect of Chongqing.
units.literal: When Shu was pacified, You was transferred to serve as prefect of Chongqing.

units.zh: 招徠撫輯，甚得民和。
units.en: He drew people back, soothed them, and won their deep trust.
units.literal: He summoned and comforted the people, gathering them in, and won the people's harmony to a high degree.

units.zh: 坐事免官，卒。
units.en: He was dismissed for an offense and later died.
units.literal: On a charge he was dismissed from office and died.

units.zh: 劉仕貆，字伯貞，安福人。
units.en: Liu Shihuan, whose style was Bozhen, came from Anfu.
units.literal: Liu Shihuan, styled Bozhen, was a native of Anfu.

units.zh: 父闬，元末隱居不仕。
units.en: His father Han lived in seclusion and refused office as the Yuan dynasty collapsed.
units.literal: His father Han, at the end of the Yuan, lived in seclusion and did not take office.

units.zh: 仕貆少受父學。
units.en: Shihuan studied under his father from boyhood.
units.literal: Shihuan in youth received his father's learning.

units.zh: 紅巾賊亂，掠其鄉，母張氏率群婦女沈茨潭死。
units.en: When Red Turban rebels ravaged the countryside, they looted his home district; his mother, Lady Zhang, led a group of women who drowned themselves in Citan Pond.
units.literal: When the Red Turban bandits rose in disorder they plundered his district; his mother Lady Zhang led a group of women to drown themselves in Citan Pond.

units.zh: 賊械仕貆，久之得釋。
units.en: The rebels put him in chains, but he was eventually released.
units.literal: The bandits put Shihuan in shackles; after a long time he obtained release.

units.zh: 洪武初，以供役為安福丞張禧所辱，仕貆憤，益力學。
units.en: Early in the Hongwu reign, while performing corvée labor he was humiliated by Zhang Xi, assistant magistrate of Anfu; stung by the insult, Shihuan threw himself even harder into his studies.
units.literal: At the beginning of Hongwu, while performing corvée labor he was insulted by Anfu Assistant Magistrate Zhang Xi; Shihuan, in anger, applied himself all the more to study.

units.zh: 十五年應「賢良」舉，對策稱旨，授廣東按察司僉事，分司瓊州。
units.en: In the fifteenth year he entered the "worthy and good" examination; his policy essay pleased the throne, and he was made vice commissioner of the Guangdong surveillance commission with jurisdiction over Qiongzhou.
units.literal: In the fifteenth year he responded to the "worthy and good" recommendation; his policy essay pleased the Emperor, and he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Guangdong Surveillance Commission, with separate jurisdiction over Qiongzhou.

units.zh: 瓊俗善蠱。
units.en: The people of Qiong were practiced in gu sorcery.
units.literal: Qiong custom was skilled in gu poison.

units.zh: 上官至，輒致所產珍貨為贄。
units.en: Whenever a superior official arrived, they would present local treasures as gifts.
units.literal: When a superior official arrived, they would invariably present the rare goods produced in their region as gifts.

units.zh: 受則喜，不受則懼按治，蠱殺之。
units.en: If the official accepted, they were pleased; if he refused, they feared prosecution and would kill him with gu poison.
units.literal: If he accepted they were pleased; if he did not accept they feared investigation and punishment and killed him with gu.

units.zh: 仕瓊者多為所汙。
units.en: Most officials who served in Qiong fell victim to this practice.
units.literal: Most of those who served in Qiong were defiled by this.

units.zh: 仕貆廉且惠，輕徭理枉，大得民和。
units.en: Shihuan was incorruptible and benevolent; he eased corvée burdens and redressed grievances, and won the people's deep trust.
units.literal: Shihuan was incorrupt and benevolent, lightened corvée and righted wrongs, and won the people's harmony to a great degree.

units.zh: 雖卻其贄，夷人不忍害也。
units.en: Even when he refused their gifts, the indigenous peoples could not bring themselves to harm him.
units.literal: Although he refused their gifts, the barbarian peoples could not bear to harm him.

units.zh: 辱仕貆者張禧，適調丞瓊山，以屬吏謁，大慚怖。
units.en: Zhang Xi, who had once humiliated him, happened to be transferred to assistant magistrate of Qiongshan and came to pay his respects as a subordinate; he was overcome with shame and fear.
units.literal: Zhang Xi, who had insulted Shihuan, happened to be transferred as assistant magistrate of Qiongshan; he came to pay respects as a subordinate official and was greatly ashamed and afraid.

units.zh: 仁貆待之與他吏等。
units.en: Shihuan treated him no differently from any other clerk.
units.literal: Shihuan treated him the same as other officials.

units.zh: 未幾，朝議省僉事官，例降東莞河泊使。
units.en: Before long the court decided to abolish vice commissioner posts, and he was demoted by precedent to river berth officer at Dongguan.
units.literal: Before long the court discussed abolishing vice commissioner posts; by precedent he was demoted to River Berth Officer of Dongguan.

units.zh: 渡河遇風，歿於水。
units.en: While crossing a river he was caught in a storm and drowned.
units.literal: Crossing a river he met wind and perished in the water.

units.zh: 同僚張仕祥葬之鴉磯。
units.en: His colleague Zhang Shixiang buried him at Yaji.
units.literal: His colleague Zhang Shixiang buried him at Yaji.

units.zh: 後有王溥者，桂林人。
units.en: Later there was Wang Pu, who came from Guilin.
units.literal: Later there was Wang Pu, a native of Guilin.

units.zh: 洪武末為廣東參政，亦以廉名。
units.en: At the end of the Hongwu reign he served as administrative commissioner of Guangdong and was likewise famed for integrity.
units.literal: At the end of Hongwu he served as Administrative Commissioner of Guangdong and was also known for incorruptibility.

units.zh: 其弟自家來省，屬吏與同舟，贈以布袍。
units.en: When his younger brother came from home to visit, a subordinate who shared the boat gave him a cloth robe.
units.literal: His younger brother came from home to visit; a subordinate official traveled on the same boat and presented him with a cloth robe.

units.zh: 溥命還之，曰：「一衣雖微，不可不慎，此汙行辱身之漸也。」
units.en: Pu ordered it returned, saying, "A single garment may seem trifling, but one must be careful—this is how tainted conduct and personal disgrace begin."
units.literal: Pu ordered it returned and said: "Though a single garment is slight, one cannot be careless—this is the first step toward conduct that stains and dishonors the person."

units.zh: 糧運由海道多漂沒，溥至庾嶺，相度形勢，命有司鑿石填塹，修治橋梁，易以車運。
units.en: Grain shipments by sea were often lost at sea. When Pu reached Dayu Ridge, he surveyed the terrain and ordered officials to cut stone, fill gullies, repair bridges, and switch to overland cart transport.
units.literal: Grain transport by sea route often drifted and sank; Pu reached Dayu Ridge, surveyed the terrain, ordered the responsible offices to cut stone and fill ditches, repair bridges, and change to cart transport.

units.zh: 民甚便之。
units.en: The people found the change a great convenience.
units.literal: The people found it very convenient.

units.zh: 居官數年，笥無重衣，庖無兼饌。
units.en: After several years in office his wardrobe held no fine garments and his kitchen never served more than one dish at a meal.
units.literal: In several years in office his chest held no heavy garments, and his kitchen had no double dishes.

units.zh: 以誣逮下詔獄，僚屬饋贐皆不受，曰：「吾豈以患難易其心哉！」
units.en: Falsely accused, he was sent to the imperial prison; when colleagues offered gifts he refused them all, saying, "Would I let hardship change what I am?"
units.literal: On a false charge he was seized and sent to the imperial prison; gifts from colleagues he would not accept, saying: "How could I let hardship change my heart!"

units.zh: 事白得歸，卒。
units.en: When the matter was cleared he was allowed to return home, and he died not long afterward.
units.literal: When the matter was cleared he was allowed to return and died.

units.zh: 時有徐均者，陽春主簿也。
units.en: At that time there was Xu Jun, chief clerk of Yangchun.
units.literal: At that time there was Xu Jun, chief clerk of Yangchun.

units.zh: 地僻，土豪得盤踞為奸。
units.en: The district was remote, and local strongmen had entrenched themselves in wrongdoing.
units.literal: The place was remote; local strongmen were able to entrench themselves and act wickedly.

units.zh: 邑長至，輒餌以厚賂。
units.en: Whenever a new magistrate arrived, they would ply him with lavish bribes.
units.literal: When the district chief arrived, they would bait him with heavy bribes.

units.zh: 從而把持之。
units.en: They thereby kept them under their control.
units.literal: They thereby controlled them.

units.zh: 均至，吏白：「應往視莫大老。」
units.en: When Jun arrived, his clerks told him, "You ought to call on the great elder Mo."
units.literal: When Jun arrived, clerks reported: "You should go to pay respects to the great elder Mo."

units.zh: 莫大老者，洞主也。
units.en: The great elder Mo was the local cave chieftain.
units.literal: The great elder Mo was the cave chieftain.

units.zh: 均曰：「此非王民邪？
units.en: Jun said, "Are they not subjects of the throne?
units.literal: Jun said: "Are these not the King's subjects?

units.zh: 不來且誅！」
units.en: If he does not come, he will be put to death!"
units.literal: If they do not come, they will be executed!"

units.zh: 出雙劍示之。
units.en: He displayed a pair of swords as a warning.
units.literal: He produced a pair of swords to show them.

units.zh: 大老恐，入謁。
units.en: Terrified, the chieftain came in to pay his respects.
units.literal: The great elder was afraid and came in to pay respects.

units.zh: 均廉得其不法事，系之獄。
units.en: Jun investigated and uncovered his crimes, then had him thrown into prison.
units.literal: Jun, through investigation, obtained evidence of his unlawful acts and imprisoned him.

units.zh: 詰朝，以兩瓜及安石榴數枚為饋，皆黃金美珠也。
units.en: The next morning he sent gifts of two melons and several pomegranates, each hollowed out and filled with gold and fine pearls.
units.literal: The next morning he sent as gifts two melons and several pomegranates—all of gold and fine pearls.

units.zh: 均不視，械送府。
units.en: Jun refused even to look at them and sent the man in chains to the prefectural seat.
units.literal: Jun would not look at them and sent him in shackles to the prefecture.

units.zh: 府官受賕縱之歸，復致前饋。
units.en: The prefectural officials took bribes and let him go; he returned and offered the same gifts again.
units.literal: The prefectural officials accepted bribes and released him to return, and he again presented the former gifts.

units.zh: 均怒，欲捕治之，而府檄調均攝陽江，陽江大治。
units.en: Jun was furious and meant to arrest him, but the prefecture reassigned Jun to administer Yangjiang, where his governance was outstanding.
units.literal: Jun was angry and wished to arrest and punish him, but the prefecture issued a dispatch transferring Jun to act as administrator of Yangjiang; Yangjiang was greatly well governed.

units.zh: 以憂去官。
units.en: He later resigned on account of mourning.
units.literal: He left office on account of grief.

units.zh: 王宗顯，和州人，僑居嚴州。
units.en: Wang Zongxian came from Hezhou but had settled in Yanzhou.
units.literal: Wang Zongxian, a native of Hezhou, sojourned in Yanzhou.

units.zh: 胡大海克嚴，禮致幕中。
units.en: When Hu Dahai took Yanzhou, he welcomed Zongxian into his staff with full courtesy.
units.literal: When Hu Dahai captured Yan, he received him with ceremony into his staff.

units.zh: 太祖征婺州，大海以宗顯見。
units.en: During the campaign against Wuzhou, Dahai introduced Zongxian to the Founding Emperor.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor campaigned against Wuzhou, Dahai presented Zongxian to him.

units.zh: 太祖曰：「我鄉里也。」
units.en: The Emperor said, "He is a man from my own country."
units.literal: The Emperor said: "He is from my home district."

units.zh: 命至婺覘敵。
units.en: He ordered him to go to Wu and spy out the enemy.
units.literal: He ordered him to go to Wu to reconnoiter the enemy.

units.zh: 宗顯潛得城中虛實及諸將短長，還白太祖。
units.en: Zongxian secretly learned the city's defenses and each general's strengths and failings, then returned to report to the Emperor.
units.literal: Zongxian secretly obtained the city's true condition and the strengths and weaknesses of the various generals, returned, and reported to the Founding Emperor.

units.zh: 太祖喜曰：「我得婺，以爾為知府。」
units.en: The Emperor was delighted and said, "When I take Wu, you shall be its prefect."
units.literal: The Emperor rejoiced and said: "When I take Wu, I shall make you prefect."

units.zh: 既而元樞密同僉寧安慶與守將帖木烈思貳，遣都事縋城請降，開東門納兵，與宗顯所刺事合。
units.en: Soon afterward the Yuan vice censor-in-chief Ning Anqing broke with the defender Temürlesi, lowered an official over the wall by rope to sue for surrender, and opened the east gate to the army—exactly as Zongxian's intelligence had predicted.
units.literal: Before long the Yuan Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Secretariat Ning Anqing turned against the defending general Temürlesi, sent a director by rope down the wall to request surrender, opened the east gate to admit troops—and this matched what Zongxian had reconnoitered.

units.zh: 改婺州為寧越府，以宗顯知府事。
units.en: Wuzhou was renamed Ningyue Prefecture, and Zongxian was appointed to govern it.
units.literal: Wu prefecture was changed to Ningyue Prefecture, and Zongxian was put in charge of prefectural affairs.

units.zh: 宗顯故儒者，博涉經史。
units.en: A former scholar, Zongxian was widely read in the classics and histories.
units.literal: Zongxian was formerly a Confucian scholar and had broad acquaintance with the classics and histories.

units.zh: 開郡學，聘葉儀、宋濂為《五經》師；
units.en: He founded a prefectural school and engaged Ye Yi and Song Lian to teach the Five Classics;
units.literal: He opened the prefectural school and engaged Ye Yi and Song Lian as teachers of the Five Classics;

units.zh: 戴良為學正；
units.en: appointed Dai Liang director of studies;
units.literal: Dai Liang as director of studies;

units.zh: 吳沈、徐源等為訓導。
units.en: and Wu Shen, Xu Yuan, and others as instructors.
units.literal: and Wu Shen, Xu Yuan, and others as instructors.

units.zh: 自兵興，學校久廢，至是始聞弦誦聲。
units.en: Schools had lain abandoned since the wars began; for the first time in years the sound of students reciting their lessons was heard again.
units.literal: Since the rise of warfare schools had long been abandoned; only now was the sound of plucked strings and recitation first heard.

units.zh: 未幾，卒官。
units.en: Before long he died in office.
units.literal: Before long he died in office.

units.zh: 太祖之下婺也，又以王興宗為金華知縣。
units.en: When the Emperor conquered Wu, he also appointed Wang Xingzong magistrate of Jinhua.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor took Wu he also appointed Wang Xingzong magistrate of Jinhua.

units.zh: 興宗，故隸人也，李善長、李文忠皆以為不可。
units.en: Xingzong had once been a bondservant, and both Li Shanzhang and Li Wenzhong objected to the appointment.
units.literal: Xingzong was formerly a bondservant; Li Shanzhang and Li Wenzhong both considered it inadmissible.

units.zh: 太祖曰：「興宗從我久，勤廉能斷，儒生法吏莫先也。」
units.en: The Emperor replied, "Xingzong has served me for years. He is diligent, incorruptible, and decisive—no scholar-official or legal clerk surpasses him."
units.literal: The Emperor said: "Xingzong has followed me long; he is diligent, incorrupt, and able to decide—no Confucian scholar or legal clerk surpasses him."

units.zh: 居三年，果以治行聞。
units.en: Within three years his reputation for good governance was established.
units.literal: After three years in office his governance was indeed renowned.

units.zh: 遷判南昌，改知嵩州。
units.en: He was promoted to judge of Nanchang and later appointed prefect of Songzhou.
units.literal: He was transferred to serve as judge of Nanchang, then changed to prefect of Songzhou.

units.zh: 時方籍民為軍，興宗奏曰：「元末聚民為兵，散則仍為民。
units.en: The court was then registering civilians as soldiers. Xingzong memorialized, "At the end of the Yuan, men were mustered as soldiers and, when disbanded, returned to civilian life.
units.literal: At that time the people were being registered for military service; Xingzong memorialized: "At the end of the Yuan the people were gathered as soldiers; when dispersed they again became civilians.

units.zh: 今軍民分矣，若籍為軍，則無民，何所征賦？」
units.en: Now soldiers and civilians are distinct. If all are registered as soldiers, there will be no taxpayers left. How then shall revenue be raised?"
units.literal: Now soldiers and civilians are separate; if registered as soldiers, there will be no civilians—from what source shall taxes be levied?"

units.zh: 帝曰：「善。」
units.en: The Emperor said, "Well said."
units.literal: The Emperor said: "Good."

units.zh: 遷懷慶知府。
units.en: He was appointed prefect of Huaqing.
units.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Huaqing.

units.zh: 上計至京，帝以事詰諸郡守，至興宗，獨曰：「是守公勤不貪，不須問。」
units.en: When he came to court to report, the Emperor questioned each prefect about local affairs. Of Xingzong alone he said, "This man is diligent, upright, and incorruptible. I need ask him nothing."
units.literal: When he came to the capital to report, the Emperor questioned the various prefects on their affairs; when it came to Xingzong, he alone said: "This prefect is public-spirited, diligent, and not greedy—no need to question him."

units.zh: 再遷蘇州，擢河南布政使。
units.en: He was transferred again to Suzhou and then promoted to administrative commissioner of Henan.
units.literal: He was again transferred to Suzhou and promoted to Administrative Commissioner of Henan.

units.zh: 陛辭，帝曰：「久不見爾，老矣，我須亦白。」
units.en: At his farewell audience the Emperor said, "It has been a long time since I saw you. You have grown old—and so have I; my beard is white now."
units.literal: At his audience of farewell the Emperor said: "It has been long since I saw you—you are old, and my beard is white too."

units.zh: 宴而遣之，益勤其職。
units.en: The Emperor gave him a feast and sent him on his way, and Xingzong threw himself even harder into his duties.
units.literal: He gave him a feast and sent him off; Xingzong applied himself all the more diligently to duty.

units.zh: 後坐累得白，卒於官。
units.en: Later he was implicated in a case but cleared, and died in office.
units.literal: Later, implicated in a case, he was cleared and died in office.

units.zh: 同時有呂文燧，字用明，永康人。
units.en: At the same time there was Lu Wensui, whose style was Yongming, from Yongkang.
units.literal: At the same time there was Lu Wensui, styled Yongming, a native of Yongkang.

units.zh: 元末盜起，文燧散家財，募壯士得三千人，與盜連戰，破走之。
units.en: When banditry erupted at the end of the Yuan, Wensui spent his family fortune to raise three thousand fighting men, battled the raiders again and again, and drove them off.
units.literal: At the end of the Yuan bandits rose; Wensui distributed his family wealth, recruited stalwart men to the number of three thousand, fought the bandits repeatedly, and routed them.

units.zh: 三授以官，皆不受。
units.en: Office was offered him three times, and each time he declined.
units.literal: Three times office was offered him; each time he refused.

units.zh: 太祖定婺，置永康翼，以文燧為左副元帥兼知縣事。
units.en: After the Emperor pacified Wu, he established the Yongkang garrison and made Wensui left vice commander while also serving as acting magistrate.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor pacified Wu he established the Yongkang wing and made Wensui left vice commander-in-chief while also administering county affairs.

units.zh: 尋召為營田司經歷，擢知廬州府。
units.en: He was soon summoned to the farming office and then promoted to prefect of Luzhou.
units.literal: Soon he was summoned as manager of the Farming Office and promoted to prefect of Luzhou.

units.zh: 浙西平，徙知嘉興。
units.en: After western Zhejiang was pacified, he was transferred to prefect of Jiaxing.
units.literal: When western Zhejiang was pacified he was transferred to prefect of Jiaxing.

units.zh: 松江民作亂，寇嘉興，文燧柵內署，帥壯士拒守。
units.en: When the people of Songjiang rebelled and attacked Jiaxing, Wensui fortified the inner government compound and led his men in defense.
units.literal: The people of Songjiang rose in disorder and raided Jiaxing; Wensui palisaded the inner compound and led stalwart men to resist and defend.

units.zh: 李文忠援至，賊就擒，諸將因欲屠城。
units.en: When Li Wenzhong's relief force arrived the rebels were captured, and the generals wanted to slaughter the city.
units.literal: When Li Wenzhong's relief arrived the bandits were captured; the generals thereupon wished to massacre the city.

units.zh: 文燧曰：「作亂者賊也，民何罪？」
units.en: Wensui said, "The rebels are guilty, not the people. What crime have the common folk committed?"
units.literal: Wensui said: "Those who rose in disorder are the bandits—what crime have the people committed?"

units.zh: 力止之。
units.en: He pressed them hard until they abandoned the plan.
units.literal: He strenuously stopped them.

units.zh: 滿三載，入朝。
units.en: After completing three years in office he went to court.
units.literal: When three years were complete he came to court.

units.zh: 奉詔持節諭阇婆國，次興化，疾卒。
units.en: On imperial orders he carried credentials as envoy to Java, but fell ill and died at Xinghua.
units.literal: By imperial order he bore credentials to instruct Java; he stopped at Xinghua and died of illness.

units.zh: 明年，嘉興佐貳以下坐鹽法死者數十人，有司以文燧嘗署名公牘，請籍其家。
units.en: The following year dozens of Jiaxing's subordinate officials were executed over salt-law violations. Because Wensui had once signed official documents, the authorities asked to confiscate his family's property.
units.literal: The next year several tens of Jiaxing's deputy officials and below died on charges relating to the salt laws; the responsible offices, because Wensui had once signed public documents, requested that his household be registered for confiscation.

units.zh: 帝曰：「文燧誠信，必不為奸利，且沒於使事，可念也，勿籍。」
units.en: The Emperor said, "Wensui was honest and trustworthy and would never have sought illicit gain. He died on a mission abroad, which is reason enough for pity. Do not confiscate his estate."
units.literal: The Emperor said: "Wensui was sincere and trustworthy and would certainly not have sought illicit profit; moreover he perished on a mission—he is to be pitied. Do not register his household."

units.zh: 一時郡守以治行稱者，又有王興福、蘇恭讓二人。
units.en: Among the prefects of that era famed for good governance were Wang Xingfu and Su Gongrang.
units.literal: Among prefects of that time renowned for governance were also Wang Xingfu and Su Gongrang.

units.zh: 興福，隨人。
units.en: Xingfu came from Sui.
units.literal: Xingfu was a native of Sui.

units.zh: 初守徵州，有善政，遷杭州。
units.en: He first governed Huizhou with distinction and was then transferred to Hangzhou.
units.literal: He first governed Huizhou with good policies and was transferred to Hangzhou.

units.zh: 杭初附，人心未安。
units.en: Hangzhou had only recently submitted, and the populace was still uneasy.
units.literal: Hangzhou had only lately submitted, and popular sentiment was not yet settled.

units.zh: 興福善撫輯，民甚德之。
units.en: Xingfu soothed and reassured the people, who came to esteem him deeply.
units.literal: Xingfu was skilled at comforting and gathering the people, and they greatly esteemed him.

units.zh: 秩滿當遷，郡人遮道攀留。
units.en: When his term ended and he was due for transfer, the people blocked the road and begged him to stay.
units.literal: When his term was complete and he was due for transfer, the people of the prefecture blocked the road and clung to detain him.

units.zh: 興福諭遣之曰：「非余能惠父老，父老善守法耳。」
units.en: Xingfu urged them to let him go, saying, "It is not that I have been generous to you; you have been good at obeying the law."
units.literal: Xingfu instructed and sent them away, saying: "It is not that I can bestow favor on the elders—the elders are good at observing the law."

units.zh: 太祖嘉之，擢吏部尚書。
units.en: The Founding Emperor praised this and promoted him to minister of personnel.
units.literal: The Founding Emperor commended this and promoted him to Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 坐事左遷西安知府，卒官。
units.en: Implicated in a case, he was demoted to prefect of Xi'an and died in office.
units.literal: On a charge he was demoted to the left as prefect of Xi'an and died in office.

units.zh: 恭讓，玉田人。
units.en: Gongrang came from Yutian.
units.literal: Gongrang was a native of Yutian.

units.zh: 舉「聰明正直」。
units.en: He was recommended in the "intelligent and upright" category.
units.literal: He was recommended on the "intelligent and upright" category.

units.zh: 任漢陽知府，為治嚴明而不苛。
units.en: As prefect of Hanyang he governed with firm clarity but without harshness.
units.literal: He served as prefect of Hanyang; his governance was strict and clear without harshness.

units.zh: 有重役，輒詣上官反復陳說，多得減省。
units.en: Whenever heavy levies were imposed, he went again and again to his superiors to plead the people's case, and many burdens were lifted.
units.literal: When there were heavy levies he would go to superiors and explain repeatedly, and much was reduced or spared.

units.zh: 而知漢陽縣者趙庭蘭，徐人。
units.en: The magistrate of Hanyang County was Zhao Tinglan, from Xu.
units.literal: The magistrate of Hanyang county was Zhao Tinglan, a native of Xu.

units.zh: 亦能愛民任事。
units.en: He too loved the people and handled affairs capably.
units.literal: He too was able to cherish the people and attend to affairs.

units.zh: 朝廷嘗遣使征陳氏散卒，他縣多以民丁應，庭蘭獨言縣無有。
units.en: When the court sent envoys to round up scattered Chen loyalists, other counties supplied civilian levies; Tinglan alone reported that his county had none.
units.literal: The court once sent envoys to conscript scattered soldiers of the Chen clan; other counties mostly supplied civilian laborers in response, but Tinglan alone said the county had none.

units.zh: 漢陽人言郡守則稱「恭讓」，言縣令則稱「庭蘭」雲。
units.en: Among the people of Hanyang, when they spoke of the prefect they said "Gongrang," and when they spoke of the magistrate they said "Tinglan."
units.literal: The people of Hanyang, speaking of the prefect, would say "Gongrang"; speaking of the magistrate, would say "Tinglan"—thus it ran.

units.zh: 王觀，字尚賓，祥符人。
units.en: Wang Guan, whose style was Shangbin, came from Xiangfu.
units.literal: Wang Guan, styled Shangbin, was a native of Xiangfu.

units.zh: 性耿介，儀度英偉，善談論。
units.en: Upright and unyielding by nature, he had a commanding presence and was an engaging speaker.
units.literal: By nature he was upright and unyielding; his bearing was heroic and imposing, and he was skilled in discourse.

units.zh: 由鄉薦入太學，擢知蘇州府。
units.en: Recommended from his district, he entered the Directorate of Education and was appointed prefect of Suzhou.
units.literal: Through provincial recommendation he entered the Directorate of Education and was selected as prefect of Suzhou.

units.zh: 公廉有威。
units.en: He was upright, incorruptible, and commanded respect.
units.literal: He was public-spirited, incorrupt, and possessed authority.

units.zh: 黠吏錢英屢陷長官，觀捶殺之。
units.en: A crafty clerk named Qian Ying had repeatedly framed his superiors; Guan had him beaten to death.
units.literal: The cunning clerk Qian Ying had repeatedly entrapped his superiors; Guan beat him to death.

units.zh: 事聞，太祖遣行人賫敕褒之，勞以禦酒。
units.en: When word reached the throne, the Founding Emperor sent an envoy with an edict of praise and rewarded him with imperial wine.
units.literal: When the matter was reported, the Founding Emperor sent an envoy bearing an edict to praise him and rewarded him with imperial wine.

units.zh: 歲大，民多逋賦，部使者督甚急。
units.en: In a year of severe drought many taxpayers fell into arrears, and the ministry envoy pressed collection relentlessly.
units.literal: In a year of great drought many people defaulted on taxes; the ministry envoy pressed collection with extreme urgency.

units.zh: 觀置酒，延諸富人，勸貸貧民償，辭指誠懇，富人皆感動，逋賦以完。
units.en: Guan held a feast for the wealthy and urged them to lend money so the poor could pay their taxes. His appeal was so sincere that the rich were moved to comply, and the arrears were cleared.
units.literal: Guan set out wine, invited the wealthy, and urged them to lend so the poor could pay; his words were sincere and earnest, and the rich were all moved—arrears were thereby cleared.

units.zh: 朝廷嘉其能，榜以勵天下。
units.en: The court praised his resourcefulness and posted his example to encourage officials throughout the empire.
units.literal: The court commended his ability and posted a notice to encourage the whole realm.

units.zh: 守蘇者前有季亨、魏觀，後有姚善、況鐘，皆賢，稱「姑蘇五太守」，並祀學宮。
units.en: The worthy prefects of Suzhou included Ji Heng and Wei Guan in the early years and Yao Shan and Kuang Zhong later; with Guan they were known as the "Five Prefects of Gusu" and all were enshrined in the school temple.
units.literal: Among those who governed Suzhou, earlier there were Ji Heng and Wei Guan, later Yao Shan and Kuang Zhong—all were worthy—and they were called the "Five Prefects of Gusu," all enshrined in the school temple.

units.zh: 楊卓，字自立，泰和人。
units.en: Yang Zhuo, whose style was Zili, came from Taihe.
units.literal: Yang Zhuo, styled Zili, was a native of Taihe.

units.zh: 洪武四年進士，授吏部主事。
units.en: A jinshi of Hongwu 4, he was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.
units.literal: A jinshi of the fourth year of Hongwu, he was appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.

units.zh: 逾年，遷廣東行省員外郎。
units.en: A year later he was transferred to vice director of the Guangdong branch secretariat.
units.literal: After a year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Guangdong Branch Secretariat.

units.zh: 田家婦獨行山中，遇伐木卒，欲亂之。
units.en: A farmer's wife was walking alone in the hills when she met lumber soldiers who tried to assault her.
units.literal: A peasant family's wife walked alone in the mountains, met lumbering soldiers, and they wished to violate her.

units.zh: 婦不從，被殺。
units.en: She resisted and was murdered.
units.literal: The woman would not submit and was killed.

units.zh: 官拷同役卒二十人，皆引服。
units.en: Officials tortured twenty soldiers who had served together, and all confessed.
units.literal: Officials tortured twenty soldiers who had served together; all confessed.

units.zh: 卓曰：：「卒人眾，必善惡異也，可盡抵罪乎？」
units.en: Zhuo said, "There are many soldiers here; surely good and bad are mixed. Can we convict them all?"
units.literal: Zhuo said: "Soldiers are many; good and evil must differ—can all be charged with the crime?"

units.zh: 列二十人庭下，熟視久之，指兩卒曰：「殺人者，汝也！」
units.en: He lined the twenty men up in the courtyard, studied them at length, then pointed to two and said, "You are the murderers!"
units.literal: He lined up the twenty men in the courtyard, studied them long, pointed to two soldiers and said: "The killers are you!"

units.zh: 兩卒大驚，服罪。
units.en: The two men were terrified and confessed.
units.literal: The two soldiers were greatly alarmed and confessed guilt.

units.zh: 坐事謫田鳳陽，復起為杭州通判。
units.en: Implicated in a case, he was banished to labor at Fengyang, then restored and appointed vice prefect of Hangzhou.
units.literal: On a charge he was banished to farm at Fengyang, then was restored and made Vice Prefect of Hangzhou.

units.zh: 有兄弟爭田者，累歲不決，卓至，垂涕開諭，遂罷爭。
units.en: Two brothers had disputed their fields for years without resolution. When Zhuo arrived he spoke to them with tears in his eyes, and they abandoned the quarrel.
units.literal: There were brothers disputing fields who for successive years could not obtain a decision; when Zhuo arrived he wept as he opened instruction, and they ceased disputing.

units.zh: 卓精吏事，吏不能欺。
units.en: Zhuo was a master of administrative detail, and clerks could not deceive him.
units.literal: Zhuo was expert in clerical affairs; clerks could not deceive him.

units.zh: 而治平恕，民悅服焉。
units.en: Yet he governed with even-handed mercy, and the people were glad to obey.
units.literal: Yet his governance was even and forgiving, and the people were pleased and submitted.

units.zh: 病免，卒。
units.en: He resigned on account of illness and died.
units.literal: He was dismissed on account of illness and died.

units.zh: 卓同邑羅性，字子理。
units.en: Zhuo's fellow townsman was Luo Xing, whose style was Zili.
units.literal: Zhuo's fellow townsman Luo Xing, styled Zili.

units.zh: 洪武初舉於鄉，授德安同知。
units.en: Early in the Hongwu reign he was recommended in his district and appointed vice prefect of De'an.
units.literal: At the beginning of Hongwu he was recommended in the district and appointed Vice Prefect of De'an.

units.zh: 有大盜久不獲，株連系獄者數百人。
units.en: A notorious bandit had long eluded capture, and hundreds of people were implicated and thrown into prison.
units.literal: There was a great bandit long uncaptured; by implication several hundred were imprisoned.

units.zh: 性至郡，悉出所系。
units.en: When Xing arrived at the prefecture, he released everyone who had been held.
units.literal: When Xing reached the prefecture he released all who had been imprisoned.

units.zh: 約十日得賊即盡貸。
units.en: He promised that if the bandit were caught within ten days, all would be fully pardoned.
units.literal: He pledged that if the bandit were captured within ten days all would be fully pardoned.

units.zh: 眾叩頭願盡力，七日果得。
units.en: The crowd kowtowed and vowed to do their utmost; on the seventh day the bandit was captured.
units.literal: The multitude kowtowed and vowed to exert themselves to the utmost; on the seventh day the bandit was indeed captured.

units.zh: 嘗治蔬圃，得窖鐵萬余斤。
units.en: While tending a vegetable garden he uncovered a cache of more than ten thousand jin of iron.
units.literal: Once, while tending a vegetable garden, he obtained from a cache more than ten thousand jin of iron.

units.zh: 會方賦鐵造軍器，民爭求售。
units.en: Just then the court was levying iron for military equipment, and the people rushed to sell it.
units.literal: It happened that iron was being levied to make military equipment, and the people competed to offer it for sale.

units.zh: 性曰：「此天所以濟民也，吾何預焉。」
units.en: Xing said, "Heaven sent this to help the people. What claim have I on it?"
units.literal: Xing said: "This is how Heaven aids the people—what part have I in it?"

units.zh: 悉以充賦。
units.en: He turned it all over to meet the levy.
units.literal: He turned it all over to meet the levy.

units.zh: 秩滿赴京，坐用棗木染軍衣，謫戍西安。
units.en: When his term ended he went to court, but was banished to garrison duty at Xi'an for using jujube wood to dye military garments.
units.literal: When his term was complete he went to the capital; on a charge of using jujube wood to dye military garments he was banished to garrison duty at Xi'an.

units.zh: 性博學。
units.en: Xing was a scholar of wide learning.
units.literal: Xing was broadly learned.

units.zh: 時四方老師宿儒在西安者數十人，吳人鄒奕曰：「合吾輩所讀書，庶幾羅先生之半。」
units.en: Dozens of eminent scholars from across the realm were then at Xi'an. Zou Yi of Wu remarked, "If we pooled all the books our circle has read, we might amount to half of Master Luo's learning."
units.literal: At that time several tens of aged teachers and established scholars from every quarter were at Xi'an; Zou Yi of Wu said: "If we combined all the books our company has read, we might approach half of Master Luo's learning."

units.zh: 年七十卒。
units.en: He died at the age of seventy.
units.literal: He died at the age of seventy.

units.zh: 道同，河間人。
units.en: Dao Tong came from Hejian.
units.literal: Dao Tong, a native of Hejian.

units.zh: 其先蒙古族也。
units.en: His family was of Mongol descent.
units.literal: His ancestors were Mongols.

units.zh: 事母以孝聞。
units.en: He was famed for the filial devotion with which he cared for his mother.
units.literal: In serving his mother he was renowned for filial piety.

units.zh: 洪武初，薦授太常司贊禮郎，出為番禺知縣。
units.en: Early in the Hongwu reign he was recommended and appointed a ceremonial officer in the Directorate of Ceremonies, then sent out as magistrate of Panyu.
units.literal: At the beginning of Hongwu, on recommendation he was appointed Ceremonial Officer of the Directorate of Ceremonies and sent out as magistrate of Panyu.

units.zh: 番禺故號「煩劇」，而軍衛尤橫，數鞭辱縣中佐吏，前令率不能堪。
units.en: Panyu had long been known as a "troublesome and arduous" posting, and the military garrisons were especially overbearing, repeatedly flogging county clerks. Previous magistrates had rarely been able to stand up to them.
units.literal: Panyu was formerly called "troublesome and arduous," and the military guards were especially overbearing, repeatedly flogging and humiliating the county's assistant officials; previous magistrates generally could not endure it.

units.zh: 同執法嚴，非理者一切抗弗從，民賴以少安。
units.en: Tong enforced the law strictly and refused every unreasonable demand, and the people found some relief in his firmness.
units.literal: Tong enforced the law strictly; whatever was unreasonable he resisted and would not obey, and the people relied on this for a measure of peace.

units.zh: 未幾，永嘉侯朱亮祖至，數以威福撼同，同不為動。
units.en: Before long the Marquis of Yongjia, Zhu Liangzu, arrived and repeatedly tried to intimidate Tong with his power; Tong would not yield.
units.literal: Before long the Marquis of Yongjia Zhu Liangzu arrived and repeatedly tried to shake Tong with displays of power and favor; Tong was unmoved.

units.zh: 土豪數十輩抑買市中珍貨，稍不快意，輒巧詆以罪。
units.en: Dozens of local strongmen forced down prices to buy up market goods, and if anyone displeased them they would contrive charges against him.
units.literal: Several tens of local strongmen forced down prices to buy precious goods in the market; if slightly displeased they would craftily slander people with crimes.

units.zh: 同械其魁通衢。
units.en: Tong had their ringleader shackled in the public square.
units.literal: Tong put their ringleader in shackles in the public thoroughfare.

units.zh: 諸豪家爭賄亮祖求免。
units.en: The powerful families competed to bribe Liangzu for his release.
units.literal: The powerful families competed in bribing Liangzu to seek release.

units.zh: 亮祖置酒召同，從容言之。
units.en: Liangzu invited Tong to a feast and spoke to him in a friendly tone.
units.literal: Liangzu set out wine and summoned Tong, speaking to him at ease.

units.zh: 同厲聲曰：「公大臣，奈何受小人役使！」
units.en: Tong replied sharply, "You are a great minister of state. How can you let yourself be used by petty men?"
units.literal: Tong said sharply: "Sir, you are a great minister—how can you be made the servant of petty men!"

units.zh: 亮祖不能屈也。
units.en: Liangzu could not sway him.
units.literal: Liangzu could not bend him.

units.zh: 他日，亮祖破械脫之，借他事笞同。
units.en: On another occasion Liangzu broke the man's shackles and set him free, then had Tong flogged on a pretext.
units.literal: Another day Liangzu broke the shackles and released him, and on another pretext had Tong flogged.

units.zh: 富民羅氏者，納女於亮祖，其兄弟因怙勢為奸。
units.en: A wealthy man named Luo had given his daughter to Liangzu, and Luo's brothers then used that connection to commit crimes.
units.literal: A wealthy man of the Luo clan had presented a daughter to Liangzu; his brothers thereupon relied on his power to act wickedly.

units.zh: 同復按治，亮祖又奪之去。
units.en: Tong investigated and punished them again, and Liangzu again intervened to free them.
units.literal: Tong again investigated and punished them, and Liangzu again seized them away.

units.zh: 同積不平，條其事奏之。
units.en: Tong's resentment mounted, and he memorialized the throne with a detailed account.
units.literal: Tong's grievance accumulated; he itemized the affair and memorialized it.

units.zh: 未至，亮祖先劾同訕傲無禮狀。
units.en: Before the memorial arrived, Liangzu had already impeached Tong for insolence and disrespect.
units.literal: Before it arrived Liangzu had already impeached Tong for insolence and lack of courtesy.

units.zh: 帝不知其由，遂使使誅同。
units.en: Unaware of the background, the Emperor sent an envoy to execute Tong.
units.literal: The Emperor, not knowing the reason, thereupon sent an envoy to execute Tong.

units.zh: 會同奏亦至。
units.en: Tong's memorial arrived the same day.
units.literal: It happened that Tong's memorial also arrived.

units.zh: 帝悟，以為同職甚卑，而敢斥言大臣不法事，其人骨鯁可用。
units.en: The Emperor understood and thought that although Tong held a humble post, he had dared to denounce a great minister's crimes—a man of such integrity could be useful.
units.literal: The Emperor understood and thought that though Tong's office was very low, he dared to denounce a great minister's unlawful conduct—such a man, with a backbone of iron, could be employed.

units.zh: 復使使宥之。
units.en: He immediately sent another envoy to pardon him.
units.literal: He again sent an envoy to pardon him.

units.zh: 兩使者同日抵番禺，後使者甫到，則同已死矣。
units.en: Both envoys reached Panyu on the same day, but the second arrived only to find that Tong was already dead.
units.literal: The two envoys reached Panyu on the same day; the later envoy had only just arrived when Tong was already dead.

units.zh: 縣民悼惜之，或刻木為主祀於家，卜之輒驗，遂傳同為神雲。
units.en: The people mourned him deeply. Some carved wooden images of him for household worship; divination through them always proved accurate, and the story spread that Tong had become a god.
units.literal: The county people mourned him; some carved wooden images as lords and worshipped them at home—divination through them was invariably efficacious—and thus it was transmitted that Tong had become a spirit.

units.zh: 當同未死時，布政使徐本雅重同。
units.en: Before Tong's death, administrative commissioner Xu Ben held him in high regard.
units.literal: While Tong had not yet died, Administrative Commissioner Xu Ben greatly esteemed him.

units.zh: 同方笞一醫未竟，而本急欲得醫，遣卒語同釋之。
units.en: Tong was in the middle of flogging a physician when Ben, who urgently needed the man, sent a soldier to order his release.
units.literal: Tong was in the midst of flogging a physician when Ben urgently needed the physician and sent a soldier to tell Tong to release him.

units.zh: 同岸然曰：「徐公乃亦效永嘉侯耶？」
units.en: Tong replied coldly, "Lord Xu, are you imitating the Marquis of Yongjia now?"
units.literal: Tong said sternly: "Lord Xu—are you too imitating the Marquis of Yongjia?"

units.zh: 笞竟，始遣。
units.en: He finished the flogging before letting the man go.
units.literal: Only when the flogging was finished did he send the man away.

units.zh: 自是上官益嚴憚，然同竟用此取禍。
units.en: From then on his superiors feared him all the more, yet it was this very stubbornness that brought about his downfall.
units.literal: From this time superiors feared him all the more, yet Tong ultimately brought disaster upon himself by this conduct.

units.zh: 先是有歐陽銘者，亦嘗以事抗將軍常遇春。
units.en: Earlier there had been Ouyang Ming, who likewise once stood up to the general Chang Yuchun.
units.literal: Earlier there was Ouyang Ming, who had also on one occasion resisted General Chang Yuchun over an affair.

units.zh: 銘，字日新，泰和人。
units.en: Ming, whose style was Rixin, came from Taihe.
units.literal: Ming, styled Rixin, was a native of Taihe.

units.zh: 以薦除江都縣丞。
units.en: On recommendation he was made assistant magistrate of Jiangdu.
units.literal: On recommendation he was appointed assistant magistrate of Jiangdu.

units.zh: 兵燹後，民死徙者十七八。
units.en: After the devastation of war, seven or eight people in ten had died or fled.
units.literal: After the fires of war, seven or eight tenths of the people had died or fled.

units.zh: 銘招徠拊循，漸次復業。
units.en: Ming drew people back, soothed them, and gradually restored livelihoods.
units.literal: Ming summoned and comforted them, and gradually they returned to their occupations.

units.zh: 有繼母告子不孝者，呼至案前，委曲開譬，母子泣謝去，卒以慈孝稱。
units.en: When a stepmother accused her stepson of unfilial conduct, he summoned them before the bench and spoke to them with gentle persuasion until mother and son wept, thanked him, and left reconciled; they were afterward praised for their renewed devotion.
units.literal: When a stepmother accused her son of unfilial conduct he called them before the bench, opened instruction with every tact, and mother and son wept, thanked him, and left—ultimately they were famed for kindness and filial piety.

units.zh: 嘗治廨後隙地，得白金百兩，會部符征漆，即市之以輸。
units.en: While tending vacant land behind the yamen he found one hundred taels of silver. When the ministry ordered a lacquer levy, he sold the silver at once to meet it.
units.literal: Once, while tending vacant land behind the yamen, he obtained one hundred taels of white silver; it happened that the ministry ordered lacquer levied, and he immediately sold it to meet the delivery.

units.zh: 遷知臨淄。
units.en: He was transferred to magistrate of Linzi.
units.literal: He was transferred to magistrate of Linzi.

units.zh: 遇春師過其境，卒入民家取酒，相毆擊，一市盡嘩。
units.en: When Yuchun's army passed through, soldiers entered a civilian home to seize wine and brawled until the whole market was in an uproar.
units.literal: When Yuchun's army passed through his jurisdiction, soldiers entered a civilian home to take wine, brawled with one another, and the whole market erupted in uproar.

units.zh: 銘笞而遣之。
units.en: Ming had them flogged and sent them on their way.
units.literal: Ming flogged them and sent them away.

units.zh: 卒訴令罵將軍，遇春詰之。
units.en: The soldiers complained that the magistrate had insulted the general, and Yuchun summoned him for questioning.
units.literal: The soldiers complained that the magistrate had cursed the general; Yuchun questioned him.

units.zh: 曰：「卒，王師，民亦王民也。
units.en: Ming answered, "Soldiers are the King's army, but civilians are the King's people too.
units.literal: He said: "Soldiers are the King's army, but the people are also the King's people.

units.zh: 民毆且死，卒不當笞耶？
units.en: They were beaten nearly to death. Should the soldiers not be flogged?
units.literal: The people were beaten nearly to death—should the soldiers not be flogged?

units.zh: 銘雖愚，何至詈將軍？
units.en: I may be foolish, but I would never insult a general.
units.literal: Though Ming is foolish, how would he go so far as to revile the general?

units.zh: 將軍大賢，奈何私一卒，撓國法？」
units.en: You are a man of great worth. How can you favor one soldier and bend the law of the state?"
units.literal: The general is greatly worthy—how can you favor a single soldier and bend the state's law?"

units.zh: 遇春意解，為責軍士以謝。
units.en: Yuchun's anger cooled; he rebuked his soldiers and apologized.
units.literal: Yuchun's mood eased, and he blamed his soldiers and apologized.

units.zh: 後大將軍徐達至，軍士相戒曰：「是健吏，曾抗常將軍者，毋犯也。」
units.en: Later, when Grand General Xu Da arrived, the soldiers warned one another, "That is the tough magistrate who stood up to General Chang. Do not cross him."
units.literal: Later, when Grand General Xu Da arrived, the soldiers warned one another: "That is the tough magistrate who once resisted General Chang—do not offend him."

units.zh: 銘為治廉靜平恕，暇輒進諸生講文藝，或單騎行田間，課耕獲。
units.en: Ming governed with integrity, calm, and mercy. In his spare time he lectured students on the classics, or rode alone through the fields to inspect the harvest.
units.literal: Ming's governance was incorrupt, tranquil, even, and forgiving; in leisure he would advance students to lecture on letters and arts, or ride alone through the fields to inspect plowing and harvest.

units.zh: 邑大治。
units.en: The district prospered under his rule.
units.literal: The district was greatly well governed.

units.zh: 秩滿入覲，卒。
units.en: When his term ended he went to court for his farewell audience and died.
units.literal: When his term was complete he entered court for audience and died.

units.zh: 盧熙，字公暨，昆山人。
units.en: Lu Xi, whose style was Gongji, came from Kunshan.
units.literal: Lu Xi, styled Gongji, was a native of Kunshan.

units.zh: 兄熊，字公武，為兗州知府。
units.en: His elder brother Xiong, whose style was Gongwu, served as prefect of Yanzhou.
units.literal: His elder brother Xiong, styled Gongwu, was prefect of Yanzhou.

units.zh: 時兵革甫定，會營魯王府。
units.en: The wars had only just ended when construction of the Prince of Lu's residence began.
units.literal: At that time the weapons of war had only just been laid down; it happened that the Prince of Lu's residence was being built.

units.zh: 又浚河，大役並興。
units.en: River dredging was ordered as well, and major public works piled up at once.
units.literal: River dredging was also undertaken, and great labor projects arose together.

units.zh: 熊竭心調度，民以不擾。
units.en: Xiong threw himself into organizing the work, and the people were spared undue hardship.
units.literal: Xiong exhausted his heart in organizing supplies, and the people were thereby not disturbed.

units.zh: 後坐累死。
units.en: He later died after being implicated in a case.
units.literal: Later he died after being implicated in a case.

units.zh: 熙以薦授睢州同知。
units.en: Xi was recommended and appointed vice prefect of Suizhou.
units.literal: Xi, on recommendation, was appointed Vice Prefect of Suizhou.

units.zh: 有惠愛，命行知府事。
units.en: Beloved for his kindness, he was ordered to act as prefect.
units.literal: He showed kindness and care, and was ordered to act in prefectural affairs.

units.zh: 適御史奉命搜舊軍，睢民濫入伍者千人，檄熙追送。
units.en: A censor was then ordered to round up former soldiers. A thousand Suizhou civilians had been improperly enrolled, and Xi was commanded to deliver them.
units.literal: It happened that a censor, by order, was searching out old soldiers; a thousand Suizhou civilians had been improperly enrolled, and a dispatch ordered Xi to pursue and deliver them.

units.zh: 熙令民自實，得嘗隸尺籍者數人畀之。
units.en: Xi had the people report honestly and turned over only the few who had actually once been on the military rolls.
units.literal: Xi ordered the people to report truthfully on themselves and gave over only the few who had once been on the military register.

units.zh: 御史怒，系曹吏，必盡得，不則以格詔論。
units.en: The censor was furious, imprisoned the bureau clerks, and demanded every man be produced or he would charge them with defying the imperial edict.
units.literal: The censor was angry, imprisoned the bureau clerks, and insisted on obtaining them all, otherwise charging obstruction of the imperial edict.

units.zh: 同官皆懼。
units.en: His colleagues were terrified.
units.literal: His colleagues were all afraid.

units.zh: 熙曰：「吾民牧也。
units.en: Xi said, "I am these people's shepherd.
units.literal: Xi said: "I am the people's shepherd.

units.zh: 民散，安用牧？」
units.en: If the people scatter, what use is a shepherd?"
units.literal: If the people scatter, of what use is a shepherd?"

units.zh: 乃自詣御史曰：「州軍籍盡此矣。
units.en: He went in person to the censor and said, "This is everyone on the prefecture's military register.
units.literal: He then went in person to the censor and said: "The prefecture's military register is exhausted with these.

units.zh: 迫之，民且散，獨有同知在耳，請以充役。」
units.en: Press harder and the people will flee. Only the vice prefect remains here—take me instead to fill your quota."
units.literal: If you press further the people will scatter; only the vice prefect remains—please take him to fill the quota."

units.zh: 御史怒斥去，堅立不動。
units.en: The censor shouted at him to leave, but Xi stood his ground and would not budge.
units.literal: The censor angrily ordered him away, but he stood firm and did not move.

units.zh: 已，知不能奪，乃罷去。
units.en: Seeing he could not prevail, the censor gave up and withdrew.
units.literal: Presently, knowing he could not prevail, the censor desisted and left.

units.zh: 後卒於官。
units.en: He later died in office.
units.literal: Later he died in office.

units.zh: 貧不能喪，官為具殮。
units.en: His family was too poor to bury him properly, and the government provided the funeral.
units.literal: Too poor to afford funeral rites, the government provided the coffining.

units.zh: 喪歸，吏民挽哭者塞道，大雨，無一人卻者。
units.en: When the coffin was borne home, officials and commoners lined the road in mourning. Though rain poured down, not one person stepped aside.
units.literal: When the coffin returned, officials and people who clung to the bier weeping blocked the road; though it poured rain, not one person stepped back.

units.zh: 又王士弘者，知寧海縣。
units.en: There was also Wang Shihong, who served as magistrate of Ninghai.
units.literal: There was also Wang Shihong, magistrate of Ninghai.

units.zh: 靖海侯吳禎奉命收方氏故卒。
units.en: The Marquis of Jinghai, Wu Zhen, was ordered to round up former soldiers of the Fang clan.
units.literal: The Marquis of Jinghai Wu Zhen was ordered to round up the Fang clan's former soldiers.

units.zh: 無賴子誣引平民，臺、溫騷然。
units.en: Ruffians falsely implicated innocent civilians, throwing Taizhou and Wenzhou into turmoil.
units.literal: Ruffians falsely implicated civilians; Taizhou and Wenzhou were in uproar.

units.zh: 士弘上封事，辭極懇切。
units.en: Shihong submitted an earnest sealed memorial to the throne.
units.literal: Shihong submitted a sealed memorial, his words extremely earnest.

units.zh: 詔罷之，民賴以安。
units.en: An edict halted the operation, and the people were spared further harm.
units.literal: An edict halted the operation, and the people relied on this for peace.

units.zh: 倪孟賢，南昌人。
units.en: Ni Mengxian came from Nanchang.
units.literal: Ni Mengxian, a native of Nanchang.

units.zh: 知麗水縣。
units.en: He served as magistrate of Lishui.
units.literal: He was magistrate of Lishui.

units.zh: 民有賣卜者，幹富室不應，遂詣京告大姓陳公望等五十七人謀亂。
units.en: A local fortune-teller, rebuffed by a wealthy family, went to the capital and accused fifty-seven leading families, including Chen Gongwang, of plotting rebellion.
units.literal: A civilian fortune-teller, rebuffed when he importuned a wealthy household, went to the capital and reported that fifty-seven men of great clans including Chen Gongwang were plotting rebellion.

units.zh: 命錦衣衛千戶周原往捕之。
units.en: Zhou Yuan, a chiliarch of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, was sent to arrest them.
units.literal: Zhou Yuan, a chiliarch of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, was ordered to go arrest them.

units.zh: 孟賢廉得實，謂僚屬曰：「朝廷命孟賢令是邑，忍坐視善良者橫被茶毒耶？」
units.en: Mengxian investigated and learned the truth. He told his staff, "The court made me magistrate of this district. How can I stand by while innocent people are destroyed?"
units.literal: Mengxian, through investigation, obtained the facts and said to his colleagues: "The court appointed Mengxian magistrate of this district—can I sit by while the good suffer arbitrary torment?"

units.zh: 即具疏聞。
units.en: He immediately memorialized the throne.
units.literal: He immediately drew up a memorial and reported it.

units.zh: 復令耆老四十人赴闕訴。
units.en: He also sent forty village elders to the capital to plead the case.
units.literal: He also ordered forty village elders to go to court and plead.

units.zh: 下法司鞫實，論告密者如律。
units.en: The judiciary investigated, confirmed the facts, and punished the informer according to law.
units.literal: The case was sent to the judiciary for investigation of the facts; the informer was sentenced according to law.

units.zh: 又樂平奸民亦詣闕訴大姓五十余家謀逆，饒州知州郎敏力為奏辨。
units.en: At Leping another schemer likewise accused more than fifty leading families of treason. Lang Min, prefect of Raozhou, vigorously memorialized in their defense.
units.literal: Also at Leping a wicked civilian went to court reporting that more than fifty great clans were plotting treason; Raozhou Prefect Lang Min strenuously memorialized in their defense.

units.zh: 詔誅奸民，而被誣者得盡釋。
units.en: An edict ordered the accuser executed, and all the falsely accused were released.
units.literal: An edict executed the wicked civilian, and those falsely accused were all released.

units.zh: 青文勝，字質夫，夔州人。
units.en: Qing Wensheng, whose style was Zhifu, came from Kuizhou.
units.literal: Qing Wensheng, styled Zhifu, was a native of Kuizhou.

units.zh: 仕為龍陽典史。
units.en: He served as the clerk of Longyang.
units.literal: He served as clerk of Longyang.

units.zh: 龍陽瀕洞庭，歲罹水患，逋賦數十萬，敲撲死者相踵。
units.en: Longyang lay on Dongting Lake and suffered floods every year. Tax arrears ran into the hundreds of thousands, and people died under the tax collectors' beatings one after another.
units.literal: Longyang bordered Dongting Lake; every year it suffered flood disasters, with several hundred thousand in tax arrears, and those who died under beating and flogging followed one upon another.

units.zh: 文勝慨然詣闕上疏，為民請命。
units.en: Wensheng went to the capital in indignation and submitted a memorial pleading for the people's lives.
units.literal: Wensheng, stirred with indignation, went to court and submitted a memorial, pleading for the people's lives.

units.zh: 再上，皆不報。
units.en: He submitted again, but received no reply.
units.literal: He submitted again, but received no response.

units.zh: 嘆曰：「何面目歸見父老！」
units.en: He sighed and said, "How can I face the elders of my district again?"
units.literal: He sighed and said: "With what face can I return to see the elders of my district!"

units.zh: 復具疏，擊登聞鼓以進，遂自經於鼓下。
units.en: He drafted another memorial, struck the Petition Drum to present it, and hanged himself beneath it.
units.literal: He again drew up a memorial, struck the Petition Drum to present it, and thereupon hanged himself beneath the drum.

units.zh: 帝聞大驚，憫其為民殺身，詔寬龍陽租二萬四千余石，定為額。
units.en: The Emperor was deeply shaken and pitied him for dying on the people's behalf. He ordered Longyang's grain levy reduced by more than twenty-four thousand shi and fixed that as the permanent quota.
units.literal: When the Emperor heard he was greatly alarmed, pitied him for giving his life for the people, and ordered that Longyang's tax be reduced by more than twenty-four thousand shi, fixing this as the quota.

units.zh: 邑人建祠祀之。
units.en: The people of the district built a shrine in his honor.
units.literal: The people of the district built a shrine to worship him.

units.zh: 妻子貧不能歸，養以公田百畝。
units.en: His wife and children were too poor to return home and were supported on one hundred mu of public land.
units.literal: His wife and children were too poor to return home; they were supported with one hundred mu of public fields.

units.zh: 萬歷十四年，詔有司春秋致祭，名其祠曰「惠烈」。
units.en: In Wanli 14 the court ordered seasonal sacrifices at his shrine and named it "Benevolent and Ardent."
units.literal: In the fourteenth year of Wanli an edict ordered the responsible offices to offer sacrifices in spring and autumn, naming the shrine "Benevolent and Ardent."

units.zh: 贊曰：太祖起閭右，稔墨吏為民害，嘗以極刑處之。
units.en: The eulogist writes: The Founding Emperor rose from humble origins and knew well how corrupt clerks preyed on the people; he sometimes punished them with the harshest penalties.
units.literal: The eulogist says: The Founding Emperor rose from the common lanes and was well acquainted with how corrupt clerks harmed the people; he once punished them with extreme penalties.

units.zh: 然每旌舉賢能，以示勸勉，不專任法也。
units.en: Yet he also repeatedly honored worthy officials to encourage others and did not rely on punishment alone.
units.literal: Yet he repeatedly commended and raised the worthy and able to display encouragement—he did not rely on law alone.

units.zh: 嘗遣行人賫敕並鈔三十錠、內酒一尊，賜平陽知縣張礎。
units.en: He once sent an envoy with an edict, thirty ingots of paper money, and a jar of imperial wine as gifts to Zhang Chu, magistrate of Pingyang.
units.literal: Once he sent an envoy bearing an edict together with thirty ingots of paper money and one jar of imperial wine to bestow on Pingyang Magistrate Zhang Chu.

units.zh: 又建陽知縣郭伯泰、丞陸鎰，為政不避權勢，遣使勞以酒醴，遷其官。
units.en: When Jianyang magistrate Guo Botai and assistant magistrate Lu Yi governed without fear of the powerful, he sent envoys with wine to honor them and promoted them.
units.literal: Also Jianyang Magistrate Guo Botai and Assistant Magistrate Lu Yi, in governing did not avoid the powerful; he sent envoys to comfort them with wine and spirits and transferred them to higher posts.

units.zh: 丹徒知縣胡夢通、丞郭伯高，金壇丞李思進，坐事當逮，民詣闕，言多善政。
units.en: When Dantu magistrate Hu Mengtong, assistant magistrate Guo Bogao, and Jintan assistant magistrate Li Sijin were to be arrested on charges, the people went to court to testify to their good governance.
units.literal: Dantu Magistrate Hu Mengtong, Assistant Magistrate Guo Bogao, and Jintan Assistant Magistrate Li Sijin, implicated in cases and due for arrest, had the people go to court reporting their many good policies.

units.zh: 帝並賜內尊，降敕褒勞。
units.en: The Emperor rewarded them all with imperial wine and issued edicts of praise.
units.literal: The Emperor bestowed imperial wine on them all and issued edicts of praise and consolation.

units.zh: 永州守余彥誠、齊東令鄭敏等十人坐事下獄，部民列政績以請，皆復官。
units.en: Yongzhou prefect Yu Yancheng, Qidong magistrate Zheng Min, and eight others were imprisoned on charges. Their constituents petitioned listing their achievements, and all were restored to office.
units.literal: Yongzhou Prefect Yu Yancheng, Qidong Magistrate Zheng Min, and others—ten men in all—were imprisoned on charges; the people of their districts listed their administrative achievements in petition, and all were restored to office.

units.zh: 宜春令沈昌等四人更擢郡守。
units.en: Yichun magistrate Shen Chang and three others were further promoted to prefects.
units.literal: Yichun Magistrate Shen Chang and three others were further promoted to prefects.

units.zh: 其自下僚不次擢用者，寧遠尉王尚賢為廣西參政，祥符丞鄒俊為大理卿，靜寧州判元善為僉都御史，芝陽令李行素為刑部侍郎。
units.en: Among those promoted out of turn from junior posts: Wang Shangxian, assistant magistrate of Ningyuan, became administrative commissioner of Guangxi; Zou Jun, assistant magistrate of Xiangfu, became minister of the Court of Judicial Review; Yuan Shan, judge of Jingning, became censor-in-chief; and Li Xingsu, magistrate of Zhiyang, became vice minister of justice.
units.literal: Among those promoted out of turn from lower offices: Ningyuan Assistant Magistrate Wang Shangxian became Guangxi Administrative Commissioner; Xiangfu Assistant Magistrate Zou Jun became Minister of the Court of Judicial Review; Jingning Prefecture Judge Yuan Shan became Censor-in-Chief; Zhiyang Magistrate Li Xingsu became Vice Minister of Justice.

units.zh: 至如懷寧丞陳希文、宜興簿王復春，先以善政擢，已知其貪肆，旋置重典。
units.en: Chen Xiwen, assistant magistrate of Huaining, and Wang Fuchun, clerk of Yixing, were first promoted for good governance but, once their greed became known, were soon punished severely.
units.literal: As for Huaining Assistant Magistrate Chen Xiwen and Yixing Clerk Wang Fuchun, first promoted for good governance, once their greed and license were known they were soon subjected to severe punishment.

units.zh: 所以風厲激勸者甚至，以故其時吏治多可紀述雲。
units.en: His methods of warning, rewarding, and exhorting officials were carried to an extraordinary degree; for that reason the governance of the age left much worth recording.
units.literal: The means by which he admonished, encouraged, and exhorted were carried to the utmost; for this reason the official governance of that time affords much that can be recorded—thus it runs.
